ArgumentOperand.description: An argument of one observed operation, valued at request time.
ArgumentOperand.title: ArgumentOperand

ArgumentValueSelection.description: The observed fact whose value the test would use for one argument.
ArgumentValueSelection.title: ArgumentValueSelection

AttackChannel.description: How the attack reaches the target agent. Structure only.
AttackChannel.title: AttackChannel

AttackPath.description:
One scenario's route to its hazard, in the order it happens.

An adversarial scenario names its attacker and steps; a functional one has
neither. The node ids are what the authoring model cites.
AttackPath.title: AttackPath

AttackPathAttacker.description: Who the attacker is, what they want, and their plan.
AttackPathAttacker.title: AttackPathAttacker

AttackPathCondition.description: One condition that must hold: the situation, an assumption, or a weak point.
AttackPathCondition.title: AttackPathCondition

AttackPathFailure.description: The observable failure and the outcome that would have been safe.
AttackPathFailure.title: AttackPathFailure

AttackPathHazard.description: The hazard the scenario reaches, with the losses it leads to.
AttackPathHazard.title: AttackPathHazard

AttackPathSource.description: A source id and its text: a violated constraint, a hazard, or a loss.
AttackPathSource.title: AttackPathSource

AttackPathStep.description: One attack step, with its ATLAS technique and the asset it touches.
AttackPathStep.title: AttackPathStep

AttackPathUnsafeAction.description: The unsafe control action and the constraints it violates.
AttackPathUnsafeAction.title: AttackPathUnsafeAction

AttackShape.description:
The structure of an adversarial scenario's attack; never attack text.

Every key is required and an absent value is an explicit ``null``.
Cross-field rules R1-R6 and R9 run as model validators; the if/then blocks
in the JSON schema mirror the ones a schema-only reader needs.
AttackShape.title: AttackShape

ConditionCheck.description:
Code-owned evaluation of a discriminating condition.

``violated`` when any comparison is violated; ``satisfied`` when at
least one comparison is satisfied and none is violated; otherwise
``not_checkable``.
ConditionCheck.title: ConditionCheck

ContentKind.description:
Closed kind of the planted data item.

The consumer chooses a concrete seed slot of this kind from the target
manifest.
ContentKind.title: ContentKind

DiscriminatingCondition.description: The model-authored condition that makes the behavior unsafe.
DiscriminatingCondition.title: DiscriminatingCondition

FailureCall.description:
The call a failure criterion is about, and how the call fails.

``incorrect_call``: the failure is a call of ``operation_name`` that is
made when it should not be, or with wrong arguments, or at the wrong time.
``missing_call``: the failure is that ``operation_name`` is not called
when it should be.
FailureCall.title: FailureCall

HandoffActor.description: The misuser of an adversarial scenario: who, and what they want.
HandoffActor.title: HandoffActor

HandoffAtlasRef.description: One MITRE ATLAS tactic or technique.
HandoffAtlasRef.title: HandoffAtlasRef

HandoffCausalFactor.description: One causal factor: its flaw and, for a belief flaw, the flawed belief.

process_model_belief.description: The controller's flawed process-model belief behind the unsafe action, or null when the factor states none: a factor that is not a belief flaw, such as a faulty decision rule applied to a correct belief, or one whose belief was not stated.
process_model_belief.title: Process Model Belief

process_model_variable.description: Present when process_model_belief states the controller's flawed belief: the variable that holds it, or a gap (id null) whose description names the variable the controller would need.

HandoffCausalFactor.title: HandoffCausalFactor

HandoffFact.description: One source-grounded fact with its authority stamp.
HandoffFact.title: HandoffFact

HandoffGherkin.description: Declarative Gherkin: no bindings, no prompt, no detector code.
HandoffGherkin.title: HandoffGherkin

HandoffHazard.description: One hazard the unsafe control action leads to.
HandoffHazard.title: HandoffHazard

HandoffObservation.description: Testability metadata without a target result or gold expectation.
HandoffObservation.title: HandoffObservation

HandoffOperation.description: A documented operation named only when it is supported and relevant.
HandoffOperation.title: HandoffOperation

HandoffProcedureStep.description: One step of the attack procedure, with its ATLAS tactic and technique.
HandoffProcedureStep.title: HandoffProcedureStep

HandoffProcessModelVariable.description:
The process-model variable that holds a stated flawed belief.

``id`` is ``null`` for a gap: no variable of the selected path holds the
belief, and ``description`` describes the variable the controller would
need.
HandoffProcessModelVariable.title: HandoffProcessModelVariable

HandoffRule.description: One governing rule the unsafe behavior would violate.
HandoffRule.title: HandoffRule

HandoffTaxonomy.description:
The ATLAS release the procedure cites and the scenario's OWASP references.

The references are the OWASP tags of the policy risks the scenario's
lineage losses came from, sorted by scheme and id, each once.
HandoffTaxonomy.title: HandoffTaxonomy

HandoffTaxonomyRef.description:
One OWASP Top 10 entry a scenario's losses map to, in its edition.

The id belongs to the scheme: ``LLMnn`` under ``owasp-llm``, ``ASInn``
under ``owasp-asi``. The schema states the pairing with one if/then block
per scheme.
HandoffTaxonomyRef.title: HandoffTaxonomyRef

HandoffUca.description: The unsafe control action in the STPA Handbook's five-part form.
HandoffUca.title: HandoffUca

IndirectShape.description: The planted-item description of an ``indirect`` attack.
IndirectShape.title: IndirectShape

ItemController.description: Who controls the planted data item, relative to the benign user and operator.
ItemController.title: ItemController

LiteralOperand.description: A literal value; a list is allowed only as the right side of in/not_in.
LiteralOperand.title: LiteralOperand

NotCalledComparison.description: The behavior is unsafe when ``operation`` is never called (an omission).
NotCalledComparison.title: NotCalledComparison

ObservationAssessment.description: Deterministic testability result persisted with a scenario.
ObservationAssessment.title: ObservationAssessment

ObservationCriterion.description: One provider-declared outcome and its requested evidence boundary.
ObservationCriterion.title: ObservationCriterion

ObservedRecordSelection.description: An observed record that meets the condition.
ObservedRecordSelection.title: ObservedRecordSelection

OrderComparison.description: ``operation`` is called without a prior call to ``requires_prior``.
OrderComparison.title: OrderComparison

PartyRelation.description: Who controls the planted item and which actor the benign turns speak as.
PartyRelation.title: PartyRelation

PlantedItem.description: The planted item: its kind and the record it lives in.
PlantedItem.title: PlantedItem

SafeCallArgument.description: One argument of the call a safe outcome states the agent makes.
SafeCallArgument.title: SafeCallArgument

SafeObservableOutcome.description:
One scenario-specific boundary for the expected safe behavior.

The statement is semantic prose, while the remaining fields bind that
prose to the exact evidence boundary supplied to Stage 5.  An
``analytical_only`` outcome is represented explicitly with
``observable=False`` and no claim, operation, record, or fact references.

``operation_name`` names the operation the boundary is about; the safe
behavior may be to call it or not to call it. ``call_made`` states which:
``True`` when the safe behavior is that the agent makes that call,
``False`` when it is that the agent does not, and absent when the outcome
does not say. ``call_arguments`` is present only when the safe behavior
is that the agent makes that call: it gives the values the call is made
with.

call_made.description: Whether the safe behavior is that the agent makes the operation_name call: true when it makes that call, false when the safe behavior is that the call is not made. Only on a command_attempt outcome that names an operation_name.
call_made.title: Call Made

call_arguments.description: Present only when the safe behavior is that the agent makes the operation_name call: the value of each argument of that call that the scenario fixes, one entry per argument. Absent when the safe behavior is that the call is not made, or no argument value is known.
call_arguments.title: Call Arguments

SafeObservableOutcome.title: SafeObservableOutcome

ScenarioDeduplicationKey.description: The stable identity used to collapse equivalent executable scenarios.
ScenarioDeduplicationKey.title: ScenarioDeduplicationKey

ShapeDowngradeReason.description: Why a proposed shape was replaced by the single-turn direct default.
ShapeDowngradeReason.title: ShapeDowngradeReason

ToolCallArgumentOperand.description: The named argument of the call assigned to ``operation``.
ToolCallArgumentOperand.title: ToolCallArgumentOperand

ToolCallCondition.description: Every comparison must hold for the condition to hold.
ToolCallCondition.title: ToolCallCondition

ToolCallConditionStatus.description: Whether the scenario's condition bound, and why not when it did not.
ToolCallConditionStatus.title: ToolCallConditionStatus

ToolCallLiteralOperand.description: A resolved value; any JSON value, including null.
ToolCallLiteralOperand.title: ToolCallLiteralOperand

ToolCallNotCalledComparison.description: No call to ``operation`` whose arguments match every ``where`` item.
ToolCallNotCalledComparison.title: ToolCallNotCalledComparison

ToolCallOrderComparison.description: ``operation`` has no earlier ``requires_prior`` call (on the same argument).
ToolCallOrderComparison.title: ToolCallOrderComparison

ToolCallValueComparison.description: ``left op right`` over the assigned call's arguments and literals.
ToolCallValueComparison.title: ToolCallValueComparison

ToolCallWhere.description: One argument equality that scopes a ``not_called`` comparison.
ToolCallWhere.title: ToolCallWhere

TurnPurpose.description: Closed vocabulary for what a turn is for. Never free text.
TurnPurpose.title: TurnPurpose

TurnShape.description: One planned turn: its position, speaker and purpose, never its words.
TurnShape.title: TurnShape

TurnSpeaker.description:
Who speaks a planned turn.

``attacker_user`` and ``benign_user`` are real user turns; the ``forged_*``
speakers exist only on the ``forged_transcript`` channel.
TurnSpeaker.title: TurnSpeaker

UnavailableRecordSelection.description: No observed record meets the condition; downstream supplies one.
UnavailableRecordSelection.title: UnavailableRecordSelection

ValueComparison.description: ``left op right`` holds when the behavior is unsafe.
ValueComparison.title: ValueComparison

description:
The versioned scenario handoff envelope (v5).

v5 carries the scenario's ``attack_path`` where v4 carries its
``attack_tree``, keeps every other v4 field, and adds ``uca``, ``actor``,
``causal_factors``, ``preconditions``, ``procedure`` and
``worst_case_threat``. ``actor`` is an object for ``kind: adversarial`` and
``null`` for ``kind: functional``; a functional scenario has no
preconditions and no procedure.

semantic_failure_call.description: The call the semantic failure criterion is about: its exact operation, and whether the failure is an incorrect call of it (incorrect_call) or that it is not called (missing_call). Absent when the criterion states no such call.

attack_shape.description: Object for adversarial scenarios; null for functional scenarios. Required, so a producer must decide.

taxonomy.description: The ATLAS release and the OWASP 2026 references of the scenario's lineage losses. Absent when the producer did not supply them.

title: ScenarioHandoff
